# Performance and visibility: build rules

Apply these rules while you build. Domains or criteria whose `applies_if` flags are false in `.quality/project.json` do not apply to this project. Before you call a task done, check your work against the criteria of the domains you touched: each one must be true and verifiable.

If a stack module of Shipwright is installed (sw-nextjs, sw-node-api, sw-vps, sw-expo, sw-capacitor, sw-tauri, sw-electron), its rules skill adds stack-specific rules on top of these.

## Performance (PRF)

Asset compression, query optimisation and speed.

Rules:

- Set a budget from the start: LCP under 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, CLS under 0.1 on mobile.
- Images in AVIF or WebP, sized, lazy-loaded below the fold, with reserved dimensions.
- Self-hosted fonts, useful subset, font-display: swap.
- No query in a loop (N+1); paginate every list that can grow.
- gzip or brotli compression and HTTP caching on static assets.
- Search and filters: send the request 250 to 300 ms after the last keystroke (debounce), cancel the previous one (AbortController), and never send the same request twice at once (a query cache such as TanStack Query or SWR).
- Read only the columns you need (no SELECT *, no full record sent to the client); log slow queries and read the plan of the slowest with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
- Remove unused dependencies (knip, free) before trying to slim down the others.
- Send requests that do not depend on each other at the same time (Promise.all, side-by-side loading), in the browser and on the server, instead of chaining them.
- Serve static files (JS, CSS, images, fonts) from a CDN or a host that provides one, with versioned names and a long cache.
- Measure Core Web Vitals on real visitors once live (the free web-vitals library, or the CrUX report): the field 75th percentile is what counts, Lighthouse only estimates it.
- A server cache (Redis or memory) only for a slow and frequent read found in the slow-query log, with its lifetime and invalidation written down; not by default.

Done means:

- [major] PRF-07: Loading holds on a throttled phone (only if: has_ui). Check: perf.json on the main pages: no failed "must" (largest paint under 4 s, layout shift of 0.1 at most, under 600 ms of blocking, under 700 kB of scripts); each "should" fixed or justified.
- [major] PRF-01: Core Web Vitals within budget on mobile (LCP, INP, CLS) (only if: has_ui). Check: Lighthouse mobile on main pages; once live, field data at the 75th percentile (web-vitals or CrUX).
- [major] PRF-02: No N+1 query or unpaginated list (only if: has_db). Check: Read data access inside loops; log the queries of one page.
- [major] PRF-03: Images optimised, sized and lazy-loaded (only if: has_ui). Check: Modern formats, srcset or image component, width and height present.
- [minor] PRF-04: JavaScript shipped to the client within budget (only if: has_ui). Check: Bundle analysis; heavy dependencies replaced or loaded on demand; unused dependencies removed (`npx knip` reports none, or each one left is justified).
- [minor] PRF-05: Compression and HTTP caching active on static assets. Check: content-encoding and cache-control headers on JS, CSS, images, fonts.
- [minor] PRF-06: API response time measured and reasonable (only if: has_backend). Check: p95 of main routes under 500 ms under normal load; no cascade of independent requests sent one after the other (Network tab, server traces).
- [minor] PRF-08: Search and typing without extra requests (only if: has_ui, has_backend). Check: With the Network tab open: a word typed in search or a filter sends one request after the typing pause, and the previous one is cancelled; on page load, no identical request is sent twice.
- [minor] PRF-09: Slow queries found, columns read limited to what is needed (only if: has_db). Check: Slow-query log on (PostgreSQL: log_min_duration_statement or pg_stat_statements); the slowest read with EXPLAIN ANALYZE and fixed or justified; no SELECT * and no full record returned on the main routes.

## SEO and meta (SEO)

Search ranking, indexing, metadata, OpenGraph and favicons.

Applies when: Public pages meant to be found on the web.

Rules:

- Every public page has a unique title and description, a readable URL and a canonical tag.
- Important content is in the served HTML (server or static rendering), not only client-generated.
- Provide sitemap.xml, robots.txt, OpenGraph, Twitter Card, favicons and manifest; a 1200 × 630 px share image, with important text away from the edges.
- Private and staging pages are not indexable.
- Choose the searches to be found for before writing the pages: one main phrase per page, taken from customers' words, recorded in .quality/project.json › seo.keywords. Two pages never target the same phrase.
- Each target page carries its phrase in the title, the h1, the description, the address and the first paragraph, in a natural sentence; never a list of keywords or forced repetition.
- Title of 15 to 60 characters and description of 70 to 160 characters, written for each page: what the page offers, then the site's name.
- sitemap.xml is generated from the real pages, lists only canonical addresses that answer 200, carries real lastmod dates and is declared in robots.txt.
- At launch: declare the site in Google Search Console (domain property verified by DNS preferably), submit the sitemap there, then check indexing; record the dates in project.json › seo.search_console.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] SEO-01: Public pages are indexable and staging is not. Check: No accidental noindex in production; noindex or password on staging.
- [major] SEO-02: Unique title, description and canonical on every public page. Check: Crawl the site and detect duplicates and gaps.
- [major] SEO-03: Complete OpenGraph and Twitter Card with a dedicated image. Check: og:title, og:description, og:image (1200 × 630), og:url; preview tested.
- [major] SEO-04: Main content present in the served HTML. Check: curl the page: main text is in the response.
- [minor] SEO-05: sitemap.xml, robots.txt, favicons and manifest present and valid. Check: Fetch each file; favicons in several sizes and apple-touch-icon.
- [minor] SEO-06: Structured data suited to the site type. Check: JSON-LD Organization, LocalBusiness, Product or Article as relevant, validated.
- [BLOCKER] SEO-08: Complete and sound sitemap, title and description filled on every page. Check: seo.json: no failed "must" (sitemap present, addresses on the right domain that answer 200 and are indexable, robots.txt not blocking the site, title and description present, unique titles).
- [major] SEO-09: Each target search has its page, and the page carries the phrase. Check: seo.json › keywords: project.json › seo.keywords declares one main phrase per page; each is in the title and the h1, and in at least two of description, first paragraph and address; no phrase targeted by two pages. Title and description lengths kept.
- [major] SEO-10: Site declared in Google Search Console, sitemap submitted. Check: project.json › seo.search_console gives the date the property was verified and the date the sitemap was submitted, confirmed by the user; the indexing report shows no error on the sitemap's pages.
- [minor] SEO-07: Correct hreflang tags for language versions (only if: multilingual). Check: Each version points to the others and to itself.

## Scalability (SCL)

Holding up under load.

Applies when: The project has a server or API.

Rules:

- Estimate expected load (concurrent users, peaks) at /kickoff and size for it, without oversizing.
- Stateless server in local memory: sessions, queues and locks in Redis or the database, so several instances can run.
- Long tasks go through a queue, not the HTTP request.

Done means:

- [major] SCL-01: Load test at expected load without errors. Check: k6 or autocannon on main routes; error rate and p95 recorded.
- [major] SCL-02: No critical state kept only in one instance's memory. Check: Sessions, real-time rooms, counters: stored or synced outside the process (Redis adapter for Socket.io).
- [minor] SCL-03: Long tasks processed in the background. Check: Email sending, file processing, exports: job queue.
- [minor] SCL-04: Database connection pool sized. Check: Pool size consistent with instance count and database limit.
